standard_position: Explicit statement that no license, right, or interest in any IP is granted or implied. Disclosure does not constitute a transfer of ownership. IP matters to be addressed in a separate, subsequent agreement if cooperation proceeds
fallback_positions: No license granted, with an acknowledgment that any jointly created IP during the NDA period will be addressed in a separate agreement to be negotiated in good faith
No license granted; each party retains ownership of its pre-existing IP; joint inventions to be jointly owned with each party free to exploit independently
red_line: Reject any clause that transfers IP ownership, grants an irrevocable license, or assigns rights to inventions or know-how arising from the information exchange
escalation_logic: Any IP assignment, license grant, or joint ownership clause must be escalated to IP counsel.
rationale: When confidential information is exchanged — particularly between engineering or R&D teams — new ideas, inventions, or improvements may arise. The NDA must be clear that sharing information does not transfer ownership of, or grant licenses to, any intellectual property.
negotiation_tips: Some NDAs include clauses that grant the receiving party a license to use the disclosed IP, or that assign ownership of any jointly developed IP to one party. Others may be silent on IP, creating ambiguity that could be exploited later.
